meta.title: About
meta.description: Veeboo AI is one technical founder in India who audits, builds and runs AI automations for small businesses. You own every account and can leave any month.

hero.title: One person builds it, and the same person picks up when you call
hero.lede: Veeboo AI is a one-person studio. I audit the process, build the automation and keep it running. No account managers and no handing your project to someone you have never met.

story.title: Who you would be working with

photo.alt: Placeholder for a photo of Aditya, founder of Veeboo AI

story.caption: Aditya, founder. Based in India.
paragraphs: I'm Aditya. I run Veeboo AI on my own, from India. I take the audit call, map the process, build the automation, test it against your real cases, and I am the one who gets the alert if something stops working.

Before the agency I built Meetbook, an AI meeting assistant that joins calls, transcribes them, writes the report and sends the follow-up. Building and running that product is where I learned what keeps an automation reliable once real customers depend on it.

I work with small businesses, usually 5 to 50 people, in the US, the UK, the UAE and Australia. At that size nobody has a spare person to babysit software. So I build things an office manager can understand: a short written description of every step, and a plain alert when the automation is unsure and needs a person.

I started Veeboo AI because small teams kept asking for the same thing: one slow, repetitive job taken off their desk, built properly and looked after. That is a better fit for one careful builder than for a large agency.
I would rather build one small thing that pays for itself than sell you a big plan. That is why every project starts with a single narrow workflow and a number we both agree to watch.

why.title: Why work with a one-person studio
why.lede: Four things are different from hiring a larger agency. Here is how each one works in practice.

items.title: One person does the work
items.text: You talk to the person who builds it. The questions you ask on a call are answered by someone who has your workflow open on the other screen.
points: Your audit call, build and support are all with Aditya
One shared channel, on email, WhatsApp or Slack, whichever you already use
Honest limit: one person means a small number of clients at a time, and a start date rather than a start tomorrow

items.title: Fast delivery
items.text: The pilot is one narrow workflow, live in 2 to 4 weeks. It runs on your real enquiries, calls or invoices, not a demo.
points: Week one: access, sample data and a written map of the process
Then a working version you can test, with changes made as you use it
The 2 to 4 weeks depends on getting access to your tools in the first few days

items.title: You own all accounts
items.text: Everything is built inside your own n8n, Make or Zapier workspace, your own CRM and your own API accounts. I am invited in as a user, and you can remove me.
points: Subscriptions and API usage are billed to you directly, at cost, with no markup
No shared passwords: access is by invitation, with its own login
Your customer data stays in the tools you already chose

items.title: No lock-in
items.text: The retainer is month to month. If you stop, the automations keep running in your accounts and you keep everything needed to run or change them.
points: A full handover document: what each workflow does, where it lives and how to fix the common faults
Workflows are exportable, so another builder or your own staff can take over
Cancel the retainer with a month's notice, in one email

timezones.title: How we work across time zones
timezones.lede: Most of the work does not need both of us awake. I build during the Indian day, you find an update when you start yours, and we keep a few live hours each week for calls.

rows.use: Calls at the start of your day
A weekly call, the rest in writing
Close to a shared working day

timezones.note: Hours shown for winter clocks. They move by an hour when daylight saving changes.
timezones.habitsTitle: What fills the hours in between
habits: A written update at the end of each working day during a build: what changed, what is next, what I need from you
Short screen recordings instead of meetings, so you can watch at your own time
Alerts from live automations go to you and to me, so a fault is seen in whichever time zone is awake
Urgent faults on a live automation are answered the same day.

process.title: The same four steps every time
process.lede: You can stop after any step and keep what has been made so far.

steps.title: Audit
steps.text: A free 30-minute call about one slow, repetitive process. You get a written plan with the cost, the expected return and what could go wrong.

steps.title: Pilot
steps.text: One narrow workflow built in your accounts and run on real work, with a number we agreed to watch.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: If the pilot earns its keep, we widen it: more cases, more tools connected, proper alerts and a handover document.
steps.meta: Scoped and priced before it starts

steps.title: Retainer
steps.text: Monitoring, fixes when a tool changes, and small improvements each month. You get a short monthly report of what ran and what it saved.

limits.title: What we say no to
limits.lede: It is cheaper for both of us to find this out now.

items.title: Work that happens a few times a month
items.text: If a task takes an hour a week, the setup fee will take years to earn back. I will tell you that on the audit call.

items.title: Decisions that need a licensed professional
items.text: An automation can collect details, book the appointment and send reminders. It should not diagnose a patient, give legal or tax advice, or approve a payment on its own.

items.title: Cold outreach at volume
items.text: No scraped lists, no mass unsolicited WhatsApp or email. It gets accounts banned and it is not the kind of work I want my name on.

items.title: Projects that need a team on call around the clock
items.text: One person cannot promise a 15-minute response at 3 am. If your process needs that, you need a larger provider, and I will say so.

items.title: Building inside accounts you do not own
items.text: If the plan only works when everything sits in my accounts, I will not build it. Ownership by the client is the whole arrangement.

items.title: A process nobody can describe yet
items.text: If the steps change every time, automating it locks in the mess. We write the process down first, and sometimes that alone fixes it.

tools.title: Tools we build with
tools.lede: Chosen for one reason: a small business can own them, pay for them directly and find another person who knows them.

groups.label: Workflow tools
groups.items: n8n, Make and Zapier. Whichever you already pay for comes first.

groups.label: AI models
groups.items: The OpenAI API and the Claude API, called from your own API account so usage is billed to you at cost.

groups.label: Voice and messaging
groups.items: Voice AI for phone lines and the WhatsApp Business API for messaging, set up under your business's own number.

groups.label: Your existing systems
groups.items: Your CRM, calendar, phone system, inbox and accounting software. The automation fits around them, not the other way round.
